schedules.title: Memory curation
schedules.description: Keeps your second brain tidy: processes uncertain or failed memory items left after archive-time auto-filing, re-checks aging notes, files durable learnings, and updates project notes when something changed. Reports only what it processed; does nothing on a quiet day.
schedules.prompt: Run this workspace's nightly memory curation. Load and follow the `memory-curation` skill — it is the complete procedure: process the proposals queue, consolidate bounded regions under the undo-log contract, re-verify aging and stale facts from `ciao memory-audit`, maintain structured learnings, keep the queue and logs separated, rotate oversized logs, and review skill proposals. Use the memory agent for vault writes. If nothing new needs processing, reply with a one-line no-op and stop. Otherwise report what the skill's report pass specifies, including every cross-project fact left queued for a bounded region, one numbered line each.

schedules.title: Install health
schedules.description: Weekly check of the parts of this install that are shared by every workspace: unresolved background job failures and pending upgrade actions. Reported once rather than once per workspace, because the findings are the same in each.
schedules.prompt: Run `ciao os-audit --json --scope global`. That scope covers only what every workspace shares: unresolved background job failures and pending upgrade actions. Exit code 1 means it found items needing attention; continue. Exit code 2 means it could not inspect required evidence reliably; report its scan errors and do not claim the install is healthy. Summarize command output instead of pasting raw JSON. Fix nothing: an upgrade action is optional and a job failure needs its own diagnosis. Report the failing jobs with their errors, the pending upgrade actions with what each suggests, and any scan errors. If the audit is reliable and clean, reply with a one-line no-op and stop.

schedules.title: Workspace hygiene
schedules.description: Weekly AI OS health check for this workspace: audits knowledge, skills, instructions, bounded memory, and unresolved automation failures, and repairs safe link drift.
schedules.prompt: Run a hygiene pass for THIS workspace only. Summarize command output instead of pasting raw JSON. Steps: 1) Run `ciao vault-index --write` to regenerate this root's INDEX.md and VOCABULARY.md from note frontmatter. The `--write` flag is required. The audit below reads what this writes, so it must run first; if it fails, report the failure plainly and do not claim the workspace is healthy. 2) Run `ciao os-audit --json --scope workspace`. It scopes its evidence to the active workspace automatically; do not pass another workspace's name. The `workspace` scope omits background job failures and upgrade actions on purpose: those are the same for every workspace and the install-health routine reports them once. Exit code 1 means the audit ran and found items needing attention; continue. Exit code 2 means it could not inspect required evidence reliably; report its scan errors and do not claim the workspace is healthy. 3) When the audit is reliable, apply only low-risk, unambiguous fixes in this workspace's vault: repair or remove dead links, fix obvious MEMORY.md drift where entries point at files that moved or no longer exist, and rename a non-canonical `type:` whose target VOCABULARY.md already names. Do not rewrite instruction conflicts, skills, orphaned notes, duplicates, invalid expiration tags, or schedule prompts. Vocabulary proposals (section 8 of the audit, informational) are also not auto-applied: a non-canonical type crossing the promotion threshold (default 5 uses) is a candidate for CANONICAL_TYPES, and a singleton near-duplicate tag (e.g. ai-analysis alongside ai) is a candidate for aliasing — both need a human decision, so report them as proposals rather than renaming them; see ciao/vocabulary_proposals.py for the threshold and near-duplicate heuristic. 4) Re-run `ciao os-audit --json --scope workspace` to verify what remains. 5) Report initial and final issue counts, what was fixed, unresolved findings, vocabulary proposals (type promotions, tag promotions, tag merges with their workspaces), and scan errors. If the first reliable audit is healthy (no defects) and the index rebuild changed nothing, reply with a one-line no-op and stop — vocabulary proposals are informational and do not by themselves prevent a no-op.

schedules.title: Skill evolution
schedules.description: Weekly look at how your custom skills performed: reviews recent sessions for errors and corrections and drafts improvement proposals for skills that struggled. Proposals are saved for your review — nothing is applied automatically, and it does nothing if you have no custom skills.
schedules.prompt: Run `python3 -m ciao.skill_evolution --min-sessions 2` with the workspace default model. Requires at least 2 failing sessions per skill (reduces noise from single-session weak signals where a skill was merely loaded). Summarize proposals written and any failed gates. Do not apply proposals automatically, and do not edit native memory unless the curation workflow explicitly calls for it.

schedules.title: Reviews hygiene
schedules.description: Daily auto-archive for Reviews helper chats (merge project fact, review proposal) that finished cleanly, so the inbox stays focused on chats needing attention.
schedules.prompt: Reviews hygiene — auto-archive completed helper chats for THIS workspace only. List active (non-archived) chats and select only chats whose title matches one of: "Merge <person> fact", "Merge project fact", "Merge memory fact", "Merge learning", or "Proposal review" (case-insensitive), or whose context is Reviews. For each candidate, use the chat metadata's active-turn flag, full last assistant response, and response status. Archive only when it is idle, has an assistant response, status is successful, and the final output indicates success — e.g. contains "Merged fact into", "dismissed proposal as promoted", "already covered", "nothing to review", or an explicit "no proposals needed" — and does not end in error, unresolved conflict, a question awaiting user input, or a needs-attention flag. Use the chat_archive tool for each qualifying chat_id. Do not archive chats that failed, asked a follow-up question, or still need user judgment. Report archived titles/chat_ids or a one-line no-op if none qualified.
